name: Spain
summary: Possessing drugs for own use is not a crime. Possession or use in public is an administrative offence (€601–30,000 fine, LO 4/2015); private use isn't penalised. Supply is criminal. Drug checking available.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Use is not a crime and health staff are bound by confidentiality; police may attend public incidents and fine public possession. Failing to help is a crime (CP art. 195).
drugChecking: Legal and available: Energy Control tests samples in Barcelona, Madrid, Palma and Antequera, and by post.

lsd.note: Not a crime to possess for own use. In public: administrative fine €601–30,000 (LO 4/2015); in private: no penalty. Supply is a crime (Penal Code art. 368).

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin is controlled and mushrooms are treated as such: public possession fined (€601+), private use not penalised; selling is prosecuted.

dmt.note: DMT is controlled: public possession fined, private use not penalised. Ayahuasca isn't listed; courts often acquit, but its DMT can be prosecuted.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is controlled: public possession fined (€601+), private use not penalised. The cacti aren't listed; selling them for consumption risks prosecution.

dox.note: DOM, DOB and DOC are UN Schedule I, which Spain applies directly: public possession fined, private use not penalised; supply is a crime.

nbomes.note: 25I-, 25B-, 25C-NBOMe are UN Schedule I: public possession fined (€601+), private use not penalised; supply is a crime.

2c-x.note: 2C-B is UN Schedule II: public possession fined (€601+), private use not penalised; supply is a crime. Other 2C-x may not be listed.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are not UN-scheduled; could not confirm a Spanish national listing. Supplying them for consumption may still be prosecuted.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT are not UN-scheduled; could not confirm a Spanish national listing. Supplying them may still be prosecuted.

cannabis.note: Private use and home growing out of public view not penalised; public possession/use: €601+ fine. Clubs are a grey zone. Medical: hospital-only (2025).

ketamine.note: Nationally controlled psychotropic (also a medical/vet anaesthetic): public possession fined €601+, private use not penalised; supply is a crime.

mxe.note: UN Schedule II since 2016, applied directly in Spain: public possession fined, private use not penalised; supply is a crime.

dxm.note: Not a controlled drug; several DXM cough syrups are sold in pharmacies without prescription.

nitrous.note: Not a controlled drug; selling it for inhalation isn't allowed, and the Balearic Islands ban recreational sale (since 2013). Possession isn't an offence.

amphetamines.note: Public possession fined (€601+), private use not penalised; supply is a crime. ADHD stimulants (methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine) on prescription.

mdma.note: Public possession fined €601–30,000, private use not penalised. Supply, or amounts beyond a few days' use, can be prosecuted as trafficking.

cocaine.note: Public possession fined €601–30,000, private use not penalised. Supply, or amounts beyond a few days' use, can be prosecuted as trafficking.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal from 18 (set by regional laws); many municipalities fine drinking in the street.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is controlled: public possession fined, private use not penalised. GBL/1,4-BD are industrial solvents, not scheduled. Sodium oxybate is prescription-only.

opioids.note: Heroin: public possession fined (€601+), private use not penalised; supply is a crime. Morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl are prescription-only.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine; not an internationally controlled drug. Selling or supplying it without authorisation is illegal.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only controlled psychotropics; non-prescribed possession in public can be fined like other drugs.

maois.note: Harmala alkaloids/Syrian rue aren't scheduled; ayahuasca is a grey area because it contains DMT. MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only.
